expectations.text: Covers all five rings as distinct sections (Earth, Water, Fire, Wind, Void)
expectations.evidence: All five present as headed sections: '地 Earth — the ground', '水 Water — the form', '火 Fire — the engagement', '風 Wind — the other schools', '空 Void — what remains'.

expectations.text: States a win condition that a third party could verify (has a number or a date)
expectations.evidence: 'By month 12 — $18,000/month gross, no more than 35% of it traceable to Local Services Ads, at least 8 named accounts..., 60+ Google reviews.'

expectations.text: Grounds the plan in the user's stated facts: two people, one truck, ~$8k/month, Google LSA dependency
expectations.evidence: Title 'A two-man junk removal outfit in Sacramento'; derives ~27 jobs/month from $8k; 'Your brother-in-law' placed as inner pillar; 'The truck is knotted wood holding up the front of the house'; LSA freeze is the central move.

expectations.text: Fire section names a specific opponent rather than leaving it abstract
expectations.evidence: Names two: 'the auction itself' (LSA) as primary, and the national franchises '1-800-GOT-JUNK, College Hunks, JunkLuggers' as secondary, with each one's cost structure described.

expectations.text: Declares which of the three initiatives (ken no sen / tai no sen / tai tai no sen) applies, and why
expectations.evidence: Splits deliberately: 'On Google: tai no sen — receive, do not attack... Everywhere else: ken no sen — attack first,' each with a stated reason.

expectations.text: Uses at most three named Fire-book tactics (does not tour the catalogue)
expectations.evidence: Exactly three: release four hands, injure the corners, hold down a pillow.

expectations.text: Every named tactic is cashed out into a concrete move, not left as a metaphor
expectations.evidence: Each carries an explicit 'The move:' — freeze LSA spend at today's dollar figure for 12 months; take storage-lien/turnover/realtor work that never enters the auction; ask for the review by name and 'text me directly next time'.

expectations.text: Water section gives a training cadence (daily/weekly/per-cycle), not just goals
expectations.evidence: Daily: live answer, walk-and-price, close-out, load log. Weekly: Friday hour, ten touches. Monthly: first Sunday, 90 minutes. Quarterly: reread and re-price.

expectations.text: Wind section characterizes at least two rival approaches concretely
expectations.evidence: Three, each with what-they-do / what-they-believe-wins / where-it-fails / take / refuse: national franchises, the Marketplace solo hauler, the SEO agency.

expectations.text: Void section names at least one specific unknown and one thing the user is pretending to know
expectations.evidence: Unknowns: real cost per job, close rate on LSA leads, whether property managers will hire a two-man outfit. Pretending: "'LSA keeps getting more expensive' is currently a feeling" and framing an idle-truck problem as a marketing-cost problem.

expectations.text: Ends with a custom Dokkodo of 3-7 terse precepts specific to this business
expectations.evidence: Seven precepts, all business-specific ('Do not raise the ad budget', 'No truck moves before the review is asked for by name'), closing with 'Number one will hurt in February.'

expectations.text: Contains no fabricated direct quotations attributed to Musashi
expectations.evidence: No quotation marks around any line attributed to Musashi; Musashi's ideas are paraphrased ('the mountain and the sea cannot be the same', 'if you let the collapsing spirit revive, it will not be a collapse') without being presented as verbatim citation.

expectations.text: No samurai cosplay: no pseudo-archaic voice, invented Japanese, or closing haiku
expectations.evidence: Plain modern prose throughout; Japanese terms limited to real ones (yotsute wo hanasu, kado ni sawaru, makura wo osayuru, tai no sen, ken no sen) used correctly.
